title: Japan Investing, FX & Visa — Fundamentals
description: Self-study deck on financial investment in Japan: FX mechanics, the tax/account framework (NISA, iDeCo, capital-gains tax), and the investor/business visa basics. Verify time-sensitive figures against current FSA/NTA sources before acting.

questions.explanation: In USD/JPY the base currency is USD; the quote is how many JPY (quote currency) one USD buys.

questions.prompt: For JPY currency pairs, one pip is conventionally:
questions.explanation: Most pairs use 0.0001, but JPY pairs are quoted to two decimals, so a pip is 0.01.

questions.prompt: Japan's FSA caps leverage for retail FX trading at approximately:
questions.explanation: Since 2011 Japanese retail FX leverage is capped at 25:1, far lower than many offshore brokers.

questions.prompt: Going long USD/JPY profits when the US dollar strengthens against the yen.
questions.explanation: Long USD/JPY = buy USD vs JPY; a higher quote (yen weaker / dollar stronger) is a gain.

questions.prompt: Carry trade in JPY classically involves:

options: Borrowing in low-yield JPY to invest in higher-yielding assets
Hedging all USD exposure with gold

questions.explanation: The yen carry trade funds higher-yield positions with cheap yen borrowing; it unwinds violently when the yen strengthens.

questions.prompt: In FX, the difference between the ask price and the bid price is called the ___.
questions.explanation: The spread (ask minus bid) is the broker's implicit cost per round trip.

options: A tax-free investment allowance for individuals

questions.explanation: New NISA is a tax-exempt investment account; gains and dividends within the allowance are untaxed, with a larger permanent framework from 2024.

questions.prompt: Japan's voluntary, income-deductible private pension program (defined-contribution) is abbreviated as ___.
questions.explanation: iDeCo — contributions are deductible, growth is tax-deferred, withdrawals are pension-taxed.

questions.prompt: The approximate total tax rate on capital gains from listed stocks in Japan (incl. the reconstruction surtax) is:
questions.explanation: 15% national + 5% local + 0.315% reconstruction surtax = 20.315% on listed-security gains via a specified account.

questions.prompt: Japan's Business Manager ('Keiei-Kanri') visa generally requires a minimum capital of about:
questions.explanation: The Business Manager visa typically requires ¥5 million in capital (or two full-time local employees) plus a real, operating office.

questions.prompt: Explain why high leverage magnifies both gains and losses in FX, and name one risk-management technique to mitigate it.

payload.rubric: States that leverage = position/margin so small price moves swing P&L on a thin margin; names stop-losses, position sizing, or lower leverage as mitigation.
